name: Hardcore Championship
epitaph: Declared “a legit title” from the ring mid-show by the fed's president at Christmas Clash '98 — a beat the crew repeated almost exactly when the UWF later legitimized its own THC — and won on the spot by Hades over Crow, the mentor of the recently-deceased Carnage. The site's own homepage, captured early the following year, names Freak the reigning champion by then.

name: Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: A three-man chain across the fed's one surviving window: Cerberus of the stable FX, Bob “Monkey” Charlie of the Youngbloods, and Jack “Big Six” Henderson, who no-showed the year-end Slammy Awards and vanished from the story before defending the belt again at Christmas Clash '98.

name: Lightweight Championship
epitaph: Todd “Ratboy” Prentiss, crowned when the division began at the In Your Computer PPV, held it through the longest uninterrupted reign the fed's recovered 1998 show recaps hold, contested against the Youngblood Psycho. The site's own homepage, captured early the following year, names Black Dragon the reigning champion by then.

name: North American Championship
epitaph: Coma's own belt before he carried the Commissioner name Joseph Rosso into the GIWF — credited a four- or five-time North American Champion as leader of the stable Crash Team, the belt's defining figure through the fed's recovered 1998 recaps, defended against Rob Williams in the Christmas Clash '98 main event billed as “two of the biggest egos going at it for North American gold.” The site's own homepage, captured early the following year, names Cage the reigning champion by then — consistent with an independent, undated title-history source whose own holder list ends at the same name.

name: Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Opens with the Warrior Clan — Akira, Tenzan, Black Dragon and company, a demonic/martial-arts stable said to have gone undefeated through seven defenses before Halloween Hell '98 — and the recovered 1998 recaps pick back up with “Omega,” Curt Raines and Scott Maestol, champions into the window until Maestol's storyline knee injury vacated the belts, the same device the GIWF and UWF would each reuse. The site's own homepage, captured early the following year, names the Hellraisers the reigning champions by then.

name: World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The top belt of the founding fed, passing through three men across the fed's recovered 1998 show recaps: Rob Williams's early two-time reign under his “Real Deal” ex-Navy-SEAL gimmick, a five-minute reign for Grim Reaper that ended on a simple clothesline, and Alien (kayfabe Chris Phillips of the Insane Crew) carrying it into a Buried Alive match at Christmas Clash '98, the year-end story those recaps close on. The site's own homepage, captured early the following year, names Lew Spectre the reigning champion by then — the last title change the surviving record shows before the fed handed over to the GIWF.
